newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rebels cut throats of five girls.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rebels cut throats of five girls.

text.p: Moslem rebels in northern Algeria kidnapped and slit the throats of five girls and butchered 14 other people in recent attacks on two villages near the capital, Algerian newspapers reported on Tuesday.

The girls were taken from their homes in Haouch Englise hamlet, in Blida province, some 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers. Their bodies were found early on Monday in Chebli village with their throats slit, El Watan reported. It did not give their ages.
Shortly before, on Sunday night, guerrillas cut the throats of 14 people from three families in neighbouring Tabainat village, said El Watan, which is usually well informed on security matters.
Security forces confirmed the deaths of the 14, saying in an official statement that they had died "in a cowardly way".

Four other bodies were discovered in Bab Ali, near Blida, while five headless bodies were found in Djebel Koukou, a guerrilla stronghold in Algiers, Liberte newspaper and El Watan said. The newspapers had no word on the identity of the victims nor when they were killed.

The latest killings followed the fifth anniversary on Sunday of the spark that ignited Algeria's war, when the army-backed authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
About 60,000 people, many of them civilians, have died since then. More than 250 people have been killed in raids and bombings, mostly in Algiers and surrounding areas, in the past two months.
Many victims have had their throats cut.

Diplomats say the rebels, fighting for a fundamentalist Islamic state, appear to be carrying out particularly gruesome killings to try to prevent the authorities from suppressing news of the conflict. The rebels have also sometimes killed girls who refused to go through forced marriages to guerrillas.
L'Authentique newspaper said security forces shot dead four guerrillas in a 15-hour gunbattle on Monday in the centre of Mostaganem town, 380 km (240 miles) west of Algiers.
